items.title: Henry A. "Hank" Kmen Interview, 1963-02-13
items.q: The interviewee mentions Don Redman only in response to the interviewer's statement ('Yeah, well, Don Redman was doing his arrangements for him before that.') and responds with 'But, uh, oh, and I don't know.' indicating no personal connection or direct experience.

ctx.x: Yeah, I don't think I would like him today, but he played in the Eysom Jones band. These are all pre-swing bands, but there were a lot of bands that played big band jazz. That didn't come out with the swing era, nor you know it's often said that that problem was solved with Fletcher Henderson when he began to write the line. He may have perfected it, but there were a lot of bands groping your way toward trying to play some kind of big band jazz or swing music before. And many bands that might be primarily…
Yeah, well, of course, if the people knew him beforehand, it never started arranging. That's what I believe, yes. Yeah, well, Don Redman was doing his arrangements for him before that.
But, uh, oh, and I don't know. Then there was a guy in the Castle Oma band, I think his name was Pat Sullivan? No, Pat… The Tenor Club?
